discovery: Direct laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of molecules

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics (ultracold molecules)
motivation: For decades, laser cooling was thought impossible for molecules because their many vibrational and rotational levels prevent closed optical cycling. DeMille showed in 2010 that molecules with diagonal Franck-Condon factors can be laser-cooled, and in 2014 his group made the first molecular magneto-optical trap. Doyle created the cryogenic buffer-gas beams that made this possible, and extended laser cooling to polyatomic molecules and to optical tweezer arrays. Tarbutt developed the theory of molecular MOTs and achieved sub-Doppler cooling and magnetic trapping of CaF at microkelvin temperatures. Together they turned molecules into laser-controllable quantum objects. This opened new routes to precision searches for physics beyond the Standard Model, such as the electron electric dipole moment, to quantum simulation with dipolar interactions, to molecular qubits, and to ultracold chemistry. It is a generic, transformative capability that now reaches across physics and chemistry.
